# Design

## A block, not a file

`AGENTS.md` belongs to the project, not to this tool. People write things in it that no generator
could know — this branch is a migration, that module is somebody else's, do not touch the theme.

So the generated part is delimited:

```markdown
<!-- hm:begin - generated by hm ai-context, do not edit inside -->
...
<!-- hm:end -->
```

Regenerating replaces what is between the markers and leaves everything else alone. A file with no
markers gets the block appended; a file with them gets it refreshed in place.

`CLAUDE.md` is different in one respect: many repositories already have one, and it is the first
thing a person wrote about their project. It is never modified. When it exists, the command prints
the single line that imports the context (`@AGENTS.md`) and lets the person put it where they
want. When it does not exist, it is created containing exactly that line.

## Generated from the resolved configuration

Every fact in the block comes from `hm describe --json`, which reads what Compose actually
resolved and what `app/etc/env.php` actually says. That is the difference between the admin path
being right and being `/admin`.

It also means the block can go stale, and staleness in a file an agent obeys is worse than not
having it. So the block records the tool version and a hash of the facts it was built from, and
`hm doctor` compares that hash against the project as it is now. An out-of-date context is a check
that fails with the command that fixes it.

## No secrets in it

`hm describe --with-secrets` will hand over the database password. The generated block uses the
plain form: the database is named, its credentials are not. Anything an agent needs to connect it
gets by running `hm mysql`, which knows them without printing them.

## One exclusion list, three consumers

`data/ai-exclusions.json` holds the paths an agent should not read, each with the reason:

| Path | Why |
|---|---|
| `app/etc/env.php` | The encryption key and the database password |
| `var/log/**` | Whatever the site logged about real customers |
| `pub/media/customer/**` | Files real customers uploaded |
| `vendor/**`, `generated/**`, `var/cache/**` | Not source, and megabytes of context |

It feeds the generated block, so an agent that only reads files knows; and `hm permissions`, which
now emits `deny` rules, so an agent whose tooling enforces permissions is stopped rather than
trusted. The two mechanisms are different in kind — one informs, one refuses — which is why both
exist and why the list is declared in one place.

Note what the last three entries are for: `vendor/` is excluded because it is noise, not because
it is dangerous. Keeping both kinds in one file with a stated reason is what keeps somebody from
"cleaning up" the dangerous ones later.

## Why a command and not part of `setup`

`hm setup` runs once per checkout and creates the environment. This writes files into the
repository that a person may or may not want committed, and it has to be re-run when the project
changes. Tying it to setup would mean either writing them for everybody or never refreshing them.
